editorial:
Imagine being told you got a huge promotion, but the catch is you have to move your entire life across a giant country without knowing a word of the local language. That is exactly what happens to Cartier, a Parisian guy living in Quebec. He is excited about the job in Vancouver, but his wife is a total whirlwind of energy who makes everything ten times more chaotic. Together with their two kids, they pile into a trailer van and hit the road. The whole vibe is a wild, wacky road trip where everything that can go wrong does go wrong, mostly because they can't communicate with the people they meet along the way.

You will love the funny chemistry between the parents and the way the movie pokes fun at cultural clashes. The pacing stays quick, though some of the jokes feel a bit dated since it came out in the 70s. If you enjoy lighthearted comedies about family stress and travel mishaps, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: After a long and exhausting trip full of arguments and language barriers, Cartier finally realizes that the corporate ladder isn't worth the stress on his family. He decides to turn down the fancy job in Vancouver. The movie wraps up with the family deciding that their happiness and sanity are more important than a title. They choose to head back home, choosing love and family peace over a stressful career move.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic road trip comedies and family chaos.
